title: TGAge: A Phenotypic Aging Clock Based on Tabular Foundation Models and the Gompertz Law for Assisted Living Facility Residents
abstract: arXiv:2610.32994v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Biological age captures overall health status beyond chronological age, yet existing biological aging clocks are difficult to apply to assisted living facility (ALF) residents due to scarce epigenetic data. We propose TGAge, a second-generation phenotypic aging clock that estimates risk-equivalent biological age from routinely collected clinical measurements. TGAge employs a tabular foundation model to predict all-cause mortality risks over discrete time-to-death intervals and converts the resulting mortality-risk ratio into biological age acceleration via the Gompertz law. We develop and evaluate TGAge on a large cohort of ALF residents curated from a proprietary, multi-state long-term care database. TGAge outperforms clinical indices and established biological aging clocks in survival prediction. Moreover, TGAge-derived age acceleration is significantly associated with multiple aging-related comorbidities. These findings support TGAg

translated_title: TGAge：基于表格基础模型与冈珀茨定律的辅助生活机构居民表型衰老时钟
translated_abstract: 生物学年龄能够捕捉超越实际年龄的整体健康状况，然而由于表观遗传数据稀缺，现有的生物学衰老时钟难以应用于辅助生活机构（ALF）居民。我们提出了TGAge，这是一种第二代表型衰老时钟，可以从常规收集的临床测量数据中估计风险等效的生物学年龄。TGAge采用表格基础模型来预测离散的距死亡时间区间内的全因死亡风险，并通过冈珀茨定律将所得的死亡风险比转换为生物学年龄加速。我们在从一个专有的多州长期护理数据库中整理的大型辅助生活机构居民队列上开发并评估了TGAge。TGAge在生存预测方面优于临床指标和已建立的生物学衰老时钟。此外，TGAge得出的年龄加速与多种衰老相关合并症显著相关。
tldr: TGAge是一种基于表格基础模型和冈珀茨定律的第二代表型衰老时钟，能够从常规临床测量数据中估计辅助生活机构居民的风险等效生物学年龄，在生存预测上优于现有方法，且其年龄加速指标与多种衰老相关合并症显著相关。
en_tdlr: TGAge is a second-generation phenotypic aging clock that combines tabular foundation models with the Gompertz law to estimate risk-equivalent biological age from routine clinical measurements for assisted living facility residents, outperforming existing clinical indices and aging clocks in survival prediction while showing significant associations with aging-related comorbidities.
